newsitem.title: GHANA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
GHANA, Aug 26 - Tema, Takoradi no berthing delays expected to Sept 9.

ISRAEL, Aug 26 - No labour problems. Haifa - seven vessels berthed and operating of which 4 discharging (2 general cargo, 2 bulkers), 3 container vessels 6 anchored of which 4 to discharge (2 general cargo, 2 to bulk cargo), 2 containers 2 bunkering, 3 under repairs/dry-docked, 3 awaiting orders,6 due, 1-2 days delay. Ashdod 14vessels berthed and operating of which 4 loading (1 general cargo, 3 bulkers), 7 discharging (4 general cargo, 3 bulkers), 3 containers. 5 waiting at anchorage of which 2 containers, 3 to discharge general cargo, 1 under repair/dry-docked, 1 awaiting orders, 1-2 Days delay. Eilat - two vessels berthed and operating (both loading) of which 1 general cargo, 1 bulker 1 Container vessel waiting at anchorage.

JORDAN, Aug 24 - Aqaba two vessels loading at berth (1 phosphate, 1 bulk dap), 13 discharging (bagged sugar, general cargo, wheat, containers, cars, meat, sulphur), 4 waiting at anchorage to load (2 phosphate, 2 livestock), 2 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE Aug 26 - Nacala - port working normally on first come, first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing at night time subject to a gratuity of $150 to be paid to the pilot. Draft restriction 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths, 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - general cargo berths working normally, first come, first served. Container/other terminals: working normally. Pilotage restricted to daylight. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation by special arrangement and restricted to 130 metres loa. Maputo - pilotage in daylight only. Two tugs, one out of order. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come, first served). Draft restriction in channel 8.5 metres less 0.5 metres plus rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Aug 26- Walvis Bay port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Aug 26 - Richards Bay - general cargo berths congested, berthing delays 24 hours. Bulk import berths congested, delays over 72 hours. Bulk export berths working normally. Bulk coal berths vessels berthing on arrival, expected to continue until 2/9. Nine vessels due before 31/8. Durban - container terminal delays up to 60 hours. Point, New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths working normally. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) two maize loaders for August, 5 for September. Citrus terminal busy in August. Delays in supplying bunkers due to bunching of vessels. Dry/floating docks fully booked for September. East London general cargo/combi terminal berths extremely busy but no delays. Dry-dock one vessel etd 28/8, one expected thereafter. Copper moving in parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month to Far East. Major problems with elevator spouts due to installation of dust extractors. Otherwise extremely busy with maize exports, delays 1-7 days. Gas oil pipeline fairly busy but can accommodate more vessels. Log loaders 15,000 CBM on hand awaiting shipment. Scrap steel 5,500 tonnes on hand awaiting shipment. Port Elizabeth working normally, 4 vessels in port. No delays general, ore, tanker or fruit berths. Container berths two vessels in port but one vessel due 2200 26/8 to wait until 0200 27/8 for berth. Cape Town breakbulk no delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal delays in week due to relocating of gantry cranes. Bunker berths 36 hours delays in coming week due to limited berths, non-availability of fuel. Drydock and repair quay full, advance booking essential. Saldanha Bay working normally.
